daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Volatility Rankings with Window Functions
daily_quests.description: Using ASX 200 historical prices dataset, calculate the 30-day rolling standard deviation of closing prices for each stock symbol using window functions. Rank stocks by volatility (highest to lowest) using ROW_NUMBER(). Then use a CTE to filter only stocks in the top 20% volatility tier and return: symbol, current_price, volatility_rank, 30day_std_dev, and price_change_pct (comparing current close to 30 days ago using LAG window function). Order results by volatility_rank ascending.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning & Aggregation
daily_quests.description: Download NSW Road Crash Data (contains crash records with timestamps, locations, severity, weather conditions). Write a Python/pandas script to: (1) Handle missing values in weather_condition and severity columns by forward-filling within each Local Government Area; (2) Convert timestamp to datetime and extract crash_hour and crash_month; (3) Remove duplicate records based on crash_id; (4) Create a new column injury_rate = (count of injured persons) / (total persons involved); (5) Export cleaned data to CSV. Validate that no nulls remain in critical columns (crash_id, location, severity). Output a summary report showing row counts before/after cleaning and % of data retained.

daily_quests.title: Australian Wildfire Risk & Climate Correlation Analysis
daily_quests.description: Combine two datasets: Australian Wildfire dataset (Kaggle) and Australian Weather observations (Bureau of Meteorology / Kaggle). (1) In Python/pandas: load both datasets, standardise date formats, merge on nearest date and location (within 50km radius using lat/lon approximation or exact postcode match). Clean merged data, handle missing values in temperature and rainfall columns using interpolation. (2) Calculate monthly fire frequency and average temperature/rainfall by region. Export cleaned merged dataset as CSV. (3) In SQL: load the merged CSV, create a CTE that ranks regions by fire frequency, then join with weather metrics. Write query to identify regions where: (fire_frequency > 75th percentile) AND (average_temperature > 30°C) AND (average_rainfall < 200mm). Return region, fire_count, avg_temp, avg_rainfall, and risk_score (normalized 0-100). Order by risk_score descending.
